# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 18 (Bi-Vb Pc18)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 18 (*Paraujjhāpanaka*) concerns the offense incurred when a nun criticizes or complains about another monastic without reflection [SuttaCentral]. In the rule's origin story (*nidāna*), a misunderstanding arose between the senior nun Bhaddā Kāpilānī and one of her female pupils; having misinterpreted her teacher, the pupil spread the claim that Bhaddā held opinions entirely opposite to her actual stance [Hüsken 1997]. As Ute Hüsken notes, the resulting rule is legally distinctive within the Suttavibhaṅga because intention is explicitly not a prerequisite for guilt: even if the criticism is voiced purely on the basis of a misunderstanding (*andersartiges Verstehen*), the nun still incurs a pācittiya offense [Hüsken 1997]. The casuistry further demonstrates that this rule is designed specifically to regulate internal monastic relationships, calibrating liability according to whether the wrongfully criticized person is fully ordained [Hüsken 1997].
In the Theravāda collection, the rule is mirrored in Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Pācittiya 18 and addressed in the Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. It has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. Corresponding Vinaya rules governing criticizing or complaining without reflection are preserved across all major Buddhist Vinaya lineages, including the Dharmaguptaka (Bi Vb Pc 87), Mahīśāsaka (Bi Vb Pc 133), Sarvāstivāda (Bi Vb Pc 94), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Chinese Pc 92; Tibetan Pc 156), Mahāsāṃghika (Bi Vb Pc 89), and Sanskrit Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda traditions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus registers 296 internal Pali text-reuse matches across 90 texts, sharing extensive shared legal phrasing with other Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules (such as Pc 19, Pc 25, and Pc 6) and Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rules, as well as automatic alignment with the Sanskrit *Śayanāsanavastu* [DharmaNexus].
